To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mast cells in the tumor microenvironment are capable of inducing collagenolysis by both tumor cells and stromal fibroblast; (2) mast cells may be involved in the selection of tumor cell subpopulations with enhanced metastatic potential; and (3) the tumor microenvironment may be an important source of collagenolytic activity.
mast cells stimulate collagenolytic activity of both host fibroblast and tumor cell populations.
the tumor-associated mast cell may be an important source of collagenolytic activity that promotes tumor invasion and metastases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of host mast cells in tumor invasion and has shown that these cells are capable of stimulating collagenolytic activity of both host and tumor cells in vitro.
the role of the mast cell in the process of tumor invasion and its possible role in the regulation of collagenolytic enzyme production.
the role of mast cell products in the induction of tumor cell and host fibroblast collagenase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mast cell is involved in the degradation of connective tissue in invasive neoplasms, and that this effect may be mediated by the production of collagenase by tumor cells and fibroblasts in the vicinity of the mast cell.
mast cell products can stimulate collagenolytic activity in both host and tumor cells.
mast cells can induce collagenase activity from both host cells and tumor cells, but the role of the mast cell in the invasion process has not been defined and remains to be investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

mast cells are involved in the degradation of stromal connectives during tumor invasion and that the host fibroblastic and tumor cell responses to mast cell stimulation are important in the regulation of tumor invasion
the tumor microenvironment, including the mast cells, plays a role in tumor invasion and that the tumor microenviroment can affect the behavior of the tumor cells.
the tumor microenvironment is an important determinant of tumor behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mast cells can be important mediators of tumor invasion by stimulating collagenolysis from both host fibrous elements and tumor cells.
the host is not just a passive bystander in tumor invasion, but is an active participant in the process.
the tumor microenvironment is a complex interplay between the tumor and the surrounding stromal cells.
